open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact legal entity (full name, legal form, and state/country of incorporation) that contracts with Tavus for speech-to-text services — Deepgram, Inc., 548 Market St Suite 25104, San Francisco, CA 94104-5401? Public registry records suggest a Delaware corporation (incorporated 2019-08-20); please confirm, and provide your principal place of business if different from the Market St suite address.

Have you designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address; if no, please state your position on why Art. 27 does not apply to your processing of EU data subjects' voice data.

Your Data Privacy Compliance page states Deepgram 'retains an independent Data Protection Officer' reachable via email. Please provide the DPO's name and telephone number and/or email address for SAP's records.

Please provide your current SOC 2 Type II report (auditor, period covered) under NDA so Tavus can place it on file (our records show no report on file in Vanta yet), plus your PCI DSS attestation. Do you hold ISO 27001, ISO 27018, or ISO 27701 certification? If yes, please provide certificate numbers and scope statements — your marketing materials reference ISO 27001-compliant environments but we found no certificate on your primary documentation.

What minimum TLS version is enforced for data in transit to api.deepgram.com and api.eu.deepgram.com (REST and WebSocket)? Your Model Improvement Program documentation states 'including TLS 1.3' — is TLS 1.3 the enforced floor, or is TLS 1.2 accepted?

Please confirm that AES-256 encryption at rest applies to ALL customer audio and transcripts stored on your systems (hosted API, both US and EU endpoints), not only to data retained under the Model Improvement Partnership Program.
Are backups encrypted, and with which algorithm? Your Security Policy documents daily backups but does not state the backup encryption standard.

Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest (platform-managed KMS, customer-specific keys, CMEK/BYOK options)? Which KMS/cloud provider holds them? One of your articles references 'customer-managed keys' for audio-retention scenarios — is that option available, and is it enabled for the Tavus account?

Can Deepgram, acting as a processor, anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer-submitted personal data (end-user speech audio and transcripts) already on your systems, on the customer's instruction — beyond the in-line transcript redaction feature?

For the Tavus account: is the Model Improvement Program opt-out (mip_opt_out) applied, and precisely what data (audio, transcripts, metadata) is retained after a request completes, for how long, when opted out vs. opted in?
For the EU endpoint (api.eu.deepgram.com): which cloud provider and EU region(s) host it, and do processing, logging, and any retention stay entirely within the EU?

Please provide your current sub-processor list for the hosted API service (we located deepgram.com/privacy/subprocessors but could not retrieve its contents) — SAP requires the processing chain to Level 2, e.g. the underlying cloud provider(s) hosting inference and storage.
